statements.quote: Aside from communication modality, all interactions were conducted under identical conditions: the same case materials, the same prompts, and the same opposition strategy. Descriptive statistics of the study sample are provided in the SI Appendix.
statements.locator: PDF p. 3, Approach, first paragraph (common case materials and supplementary descriptives).

statements.quote: This observed switch rate is statistically indistinguishable from a benchmark of independent, equal-probability draws at each such session (two-sided exact test, p = 0.14; details provided in the SI Appendix).
statements.locator: PDF p. 3, Approach, second paragraph (supplementary modality-switching analysis).

statements.quote: Full transcripts of each interaction are provided in the SI Appendix.
statements.locator: PDF p. 4, Findings, paragraph introducing the two representative Netflix interactions; transcripts appear on pp. 12-16.

statements.quote: All data analysis was conducted using the R statistical software. The SI Appendix contains additional information on measure construction, including the calculation of lexical and semantic diversity. Anonymized data and code to replicate all findings are available for this manuscript.
statements.locator: PDF p. 6, Materials and Methods, final three sentences (analysis software, SI Appendix and data/code availability).

statements.quote: User messages were extracted from CAiSEY conversation transcripts by identifying lines prefixed with "USER:" and concatenating them. All text measures were computed on these user-only texts.
statements.locator: PDF p. 11, Supporting Information, Text Extraction (description of underlying transcript data, not an access location).

statements.quote: All regressions were implemented in the R statistical software. They are ordinary least-squares regressions with user and case fixed effects and robust standard errors clustered at the user and case levels.
statements.locator: PDF p. 12, Supporting Information, Statistical Analyses (software statement, not a code repository).

notes: Checked on 2026-10-09. Read the entire saved markdown conversion (44000 characters, 330 lines), including Supporting Information and both complete representative transcripts, and checked the quoted passages against PDF text. Quotes preserve source wording with PDF line-break whitespace normalized. The availability statement on PDF p. 6 says anonymized data and replication code are available but provides no repository name, URL, DOI, access procedure, or explicit on-request condition. The screening form data_and_code contains data_url=null and code_url=null. No preregistration statement, repository link, separate supplementary-file download, or embedded PDF attachment was found. All network checks used Python urllib and User-Agent atlas-screening/0.1, without an email address, login or access request. Link checks: https://caisey.me/demo (printed on p. 12) returned HTTP 429 with a Vercel Security Checkpoint; the embedded hyperlink https://www.caisey.me/demo also returned HTTP 429 with that checkpoint. No attempt was made to pass either checkpoint. The paper describes this as a live demonstration, so it is not counted as a data/code deposit; its files and actual access conditions remain unconfirmed. The other printed URL, http://arxiv.org/abs/2409.01754 (p. 7, reference 6), returned HTTP 200 after redirecting to https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.01754. It concerns a different paper by Yakura and colleagues, not this study or its data. The source landing page https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.27073 returned HTTP 200. It lists only v1, submitted 28 March 2026, with 16 pages, one figure and one table, and links to the paper PDF; no article-specific data/code/supplementary-file URL or journal-publisher version is listed. Generic arXiv code/data service toggles are not deposits. The public PDF https://arxiv.org/pdf/2603.27073 returned HTTP 200, was read only in memory (1194844 bytes, 16 pages), and is byte-for-byte identical to the saved PDF. Its arXiv/DataCite license is CC BY 4.0; this does not establish a license or location for an unpublished dataset. The manuscript contains two selected illustrative transcripts labeled USER105 (text; pp. 12-14) and USER015 (voice; pp. 14-16), with some individual example scores in Findings (pp. 4-5). These in-article illustrations are not counted as a participant-data deposit. They omit the randomized male/female voice assignment, the full conversation panel and the participant-linked outcome matrix. They cannot establish analyzed counts by modality or voice gender, per-person arm means/SDs/SEs, voice-gender estimates and uncertainty, or sample-level diversity measures. No downloadable analysis file was found and no data-file rows or columns were available to inspect. Search endpoints were https://api.datacite.org/dois?query=..., https://zenodo.org/api/records?q=..., https://dataverse.harvard.edu/api/search?q=..., and https://api.osf.io/v2/nodes/?filter[title]=.... Result counts are API-reported totals, not counts of relevant deposits. All required title and first-author searches completed; additional variants and their limitations are recorded in searches. No named relevant GitHub repository or OSF/Dataverse/Zenodo/Dryad/Figshare deposit was found, so no relevant repository file inventory could be obtained. Status none_found means no public analysis-data deposit was located in these checks, not proof that none exists. The paper does not say data are available on request, so on_request would be unsupported. The missing repository location remains unresolved, as do the form final.open_items concerning distinct-person counts, voice-gender results and the lexical-diversity specification discrepancy. Confidence is medium because the manuscript asserts availability without an access location, the demo could not be inspected, OSF searches were limited to the supplied title-filter endpoint, and the broad DataCite AND query was only partly reviewed.
